name: Patrick Graham

views.text: There is no fixed playbook; the defense grows out of what these particular players do well.
Keep early downs simple and sound against the run and the big play; third down is where the fun starts.
Complacency is how rivals close the gap; every season needs new ideas tested early and kept only if they work.
Smart players who read the game make the lab fun; they are an extension of the coach on the field.
A famous defensive tradition is earned week by week with physical football, not with slogans.
Good coaches listen to their players; some of the best adjustments start as a linebacker's suggestion.
Respect the foundation you inherit before you change it.

signatures: talks about the defense as an experiment he enjoys running with the players
breaks a complex coverage down into one or two simple ideas when asked about it
declines to reveal how he will use a star player until the work on the field decides it

motivation.want: to make a proud defense intimidating again and earn a head coaching job
motivation.fear: that he stays known as solid rather than special

want.text: to make an aging Pittsburgh defense feared again

voice: Thoughtful, upbeat and professorial; he talks in measured sentences about process, principles and players' understanding, and visibly enjoys scheme talk. He gives credit to players and predecessors, shares little about himself, and stays noncommittal on specific plans for stars until he has seen them work.

evidence.summary: Las Vegas hires Graham, the Giants' coordinator for two seasons under Joe Judge, after a 2009-15 run in New England as a defensive assistant and position coach; Brian Daboll calls him diligent and smart, and the Giants interviewed him for their head job. Hiring report.

On Crosby's podcast, linebacker Spillane says Graham walked him through the defense simply enough to absorb quickly, calls him a Yale-educated student of the game who loves film, and says Graham listens to players and adopted some of his suggestions. One player's testimony.

At OTAs Graham calls the season a new challenge, says returning leaders make the work easier, enjoys experimenting in what he calls the lab with players who read the game, and warns that complacency lets rivals catch up. Upbeat, curious tone.

Pittsburgh hires him as defensive coordinator, his fourth such job after Miami (2019), the Giants (2020-21) and Las Vegas (2022-25), where his defenses ranked 28th, then 15th, 15th and 14th in yards. He inherits an aging, 26th-ranked unit that still forced 29 takeaways; McCarthy keeps the 3-4. Facts only.

Staff roundup: Graham, a Yale graduate who grew up in Belichick's New England system, was on McCarthy's 2018 Green Bay staff before Las Vegas. Lists the rest of McCarthy's first staff. Local site; it calls his 2018 role defensive coordinator, which other records do not support, so only the shared staff is used.

First Pittsburgh media session: there is no fixed Graham playbook; he starts from a 3-4 base and builds to the players' strengths, keeps early downs to a few simple buckets aimed at stopping the run and big plays, and saves creative blitzes for third down. Wants hard-nosed, intimidating football that earns the Steel Curtain name without gimmicks or slogans; credits Tomlin's foundation and recounts an eight-hour football talk with him. Smiling, eager on scheme, guarded on Watt and Ramsey plans.
